summary_en: This Phase 2/3 study compares datopotamab deruxtecan plus carboplatin or cisplatin with gemcitabine plus carboplatin or cisplatin in urothelial carcinoma that has progressed during or after enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab. Datopotamab deruxtecan is given by IV infusion every three weeks at 4 mg/kg or 6 mg/kg, and the comparison arm gets gemcitabine on Days 1 and 8 of each three-week cycle; how long treatment continues is not stated. The record does not state a primary outcome, but Part A (Phase 2) assesses preliminary efficacy and safety, and the Phase 3 part starts depending on Phase 2 results.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2/3 compara datopotamab deruxtecan más carboplatino o cisplatino con gemcitabina más carboplatino o cisplatino en carcinoma urotelial que progresó durante o después de enfortumab vedotina y pembrolizumab. El datopotamab deruxtecan se administra por infusión intravenosa cada tres semanas a 4 mg/kg o 6 mg/kg, y el brazo de comparación recibe gemcitabina los días 1 y 8 de cada ciclo de tres semanas; el registro no indica cuánto tiempo continúa el tratamiento. El registro no indica un desenlace principal, pero la Parte A (fase 2) evalúa la eficacia preliminar y la seguridad, y la parte de fase 3 comienza según los resultados de la fase 2.
who_for: Unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
Radiographic progression during or after first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (or similar agents).
Considered eligible for cisplatin- or carboplatin-containing chemotherapy by the investigator.
Must provide a tumor tissue sample for biomarker testing.
not_for: Prior systemic therapy for advanced disease other than enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, with some exceptions needing sponsor approval.
History of allogeneic bone marrow or solid organ transplant.
Uncontrolled or significant cardiovascular disease, including QTcF above 470 ms.
History of non-infectious interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis requiring steroids, or current or suspected ILD/pneumonitis.
